title: Da Hook
canon: Dashiell Hammett's The Maltese Falcon (1930, public domain) transposed to Red Hook, Brooklyn, in the fall of 1970 — the Knicks' first championship banner is fresh, the World Trade Center's bare steel is climbing past the Empire State Building, the piers are dying underneath it, and the heroin epidemic is cresting. An unreadable investigator — per the working skeleton a marine-claims man walking the piers, not a private eye — loses his partner to a murder over a legendary lost prize, follows a lying client through a fixer, a collector, and a false MacGuffin, and turns in the woman he loves because his code allows no other end. New Renaissance Cinema feature.
look: French Connection austerity: documentary grit, handheld grammar, no glamour, no golden hour. Hard-shadow noir geometry — single or dual directional sources, deep blacks, clean whites, no fill that softens the shadow. Moderate telephoto character (50-85mm), 35mm grain present but not heavy, muted desaturated late-autumn palette. Period-precise fall 1970: WTC is bare steel under cranes and NEVER completed towers, no post-1970 vehicles, no 1940s trench-coat/fedora Bogart aesthetic — this detective looks like he works for a living.
note: Light Law pass 2026-07-18 — prompts from macguffin-1973-reframe-skeleton-draft-1.md. TRANSLATION RULE: the skeleton is written to spring 1973, but the property's period canon is fall 1970 (re-ruled 2026-07-10, per the old spec and reference-on-sharedData.md), so the skeleton's 1973 texture is translated — first Knicks championship afterglow (never the second title), WTC bare steel under kangaroo cranes (never completed or open towers). COLOR RULING CARRIED FORWARD, STILL OPEN: the Gate-1 brief locks B&W period-precise as interim default, but the entire generated set to date is desaturated Eastman color; these prompts are written in muted color to match the set — Marco must rule B&W vs color before a full regen. MACGUFFIN AGNOSTIC per the open ruling: the stolen French Connection heroin / property-voucher proposal (skeleton Part 1) is unruled, so no contraband is ever depicted — the prize appears only as a legend told aloud. CHARACTER NAMES pending the 1939-film recast (skeleton Part 2, unruled) — every figure is described by role, never named. NO cast face is locked; 05-investigator.png remains banned (fedora/trench wardrobe); reference-manifest.md (checked 2026-07-18) carries no current cast refs, so refs are empty on all eight shots. Standard (Marco 2026-07-18): each shot is a moment in time — a touch, an embrace, a tear, a look held too long — human emotion is the story, not action. All eight are distinct from the twelve shots in specs/11-04-da-hook.json.

stills.notes: Open ruling 7 ('Which exact frame … a longshoreman's shape-up') + Part 5: 'the break-bulk piers, the multi-story warehouses, the longshore jobs were dying.' The dying-waterfront weather compressed into one man's face — the moment of not being chosen, with the steel that replaced him in the same frame.
stills.prompt: Dawn shape-up outside a shuttered pier shed off Beard Street, Red Hook, Brooklyn, fall 1970. A hiring boss on a crate points men through the gate and a knot of chosen longshoremen file past with cargo hooks over their shoulders. Apart from them stands an older longshoreman the pointing finger skipped, hook still on his shoulder, thermos under his arm, and his face carries the whole story: a working man understanding the work is over. Across the Upper Bay the bare steel of the World Trade Center climbs unfinished under kangaroo cranes. The light is grey-pink harbor dawn off the water and one sodium lamp still burning under the shed eave, warm against the cold sky. Grainy 35mm Eastman color negative, muted late-autumn palette, full-bleed frame, no black bars, no text, no watermark.

stills.notes: Skeleton reframe of Hammett ch. 2 (the night telephone call that the partner is dead), lead per Part 3 S1: 'a company man with a code.' The death lands in a stopped hand and a white-knuckle grip, not in action — the murder itself is already covered by partner-dead-on-the-docks in the old spec; this is the moment it reaches him.
stills.prompt: A walk-up bedroom off Court Street, Carroll Gardens, Brooklyn, fall 1970, two in the morning. The marine-claims investigator, early forties, sits on the edge of an unmade bed in an undershirt, black rotary receiver pressed to his ear, being told his partner is dead. His face gives nothing. His free hand, caught mid-roll on a cigarette, has stopped moving, tobacco spilling from the paper, and his knuckles are white on the receiver. No lamp is on. The only light is sodium streetlight coming up through the venetian blinds, laying broken orange bands across the bedclothes and one side of his face; the rest of the room falls to black. Grainy 35mm Eastman color negative pushed for the low light, muted palette, full-bleed frame, no black bars, no text, no watermark.

stills.notes: Skeleton reframe of Hammett ch. 3 ('Three Women' — the widow comes to the office the morning after), roles per Part 2: 'the partner's widow, the lead's affair' and 'the loyal secretary / the lead's conscience.' The guilt of the affair is told entirely by the hand that will not land on her back, and by the secretary seeing it.
stills.prompt: The second-floor office above a dry cleaner in Carroll Gardens, Brooklyn, fall 1970, the morning after the murder. The dead partner's widow, in black with her veil pushed back, presses her face into the investigator's chest, fists closed on his lapels, shaking. His arms stay at his sides; one hand has risen halfway toward her back and stopped there, not landing. Over her shoulder, in the frosted-glass doorway, the young secretary stands holding the morning mail and watches that suspended hand. Hard morning sun through the venetian blinds rakes slat shadows across the two of them, and the small tungsten desk lamp burns at frame edge. Grainy 35mm Eastman color negative, muted desaturated palette, full-bleed frame, no black bars, no text, no watermark.

stills.notes: Skeleton reframe of Hammett ch. 9 ('Brigid' — the tired-of-lying confession), role per Part 2: 'the client, the liar.' A touch held too long that reads two ways at once: she performs surrender with the tears, and his eyes audit the performance — the whole relationship in one held gesture.
stills.prompt: A furnished rooming-house bedroom near the Brooklyn Heights end of Clinton Street, fall 1970, night. A young dark-haired woman in a slip and cardigan sits on the edge of the bed mid-confession, tears on her face, holding the investigator's hand against her wet cheek with both of hers. He stands over her and lets her hold it, and his eyes are not comforting her; they are measuring her. The room's only lights are a small bedside lamp with a scorched paper shade and the sodium streetlight through the lace curtains, two color temperatures crossing on the bed, the corners of the room gone dark. Grainy 35mm Eastman color negative, muted palette, full-bleed frame, no black bars, no text, no watermark.

stills.notes: Part 1, 'The legend speech (Gutman's history aria, transposed)': 'Marseille, the freighter, the seizure, the courtroom, the property clerk, the weevils, the cover-up … the myth of the one brick that got away.' The emotion is the believer's rapture; MacGuffin stays agnostic — nothing is depicted but the telling. Same Hotel St. George geography as the old spec's laced-glass shot, different night, different beat.
stills.prompt: A high-floor suite in the Hotel St. George, Brooklyn Heights, fall 1970, night. A vast composed older man in an expensive three-piece suit leans forward out of a wing armchair, mid-story, whiskey forgotten on the armrest, both hands shaping a freighter in the air, and his face is lit from inside by pure belief: he is reciting the legend of the one prize that got away. Across the low table the marine-claims investigator watches the man, not the hands, reading the believer instead of the story. The room's own fixtures do all the lighting: one fringed floor lamp beside the armchair, a low table lamp, and the cold blue harbor night through the window sheers, deep shadow between the sources. Grainy 35mm Eastman color negative, muted palette, full-bleed frame, no black bars, no text, no watermark.

stills.notes: Part 5, the Knicks engine: 'A pass-first, unselfish team … "the way the game ought to be played" … which sits as a silent rebuke over a story where everyone sells out everyone for a brick of flour.' Skeleton's 1973 second title translated to the fall-1970 first-championship canon per the period re-ruling. The city's joy fills the room; the man the story owns sits outside it.
stills.prompt: A longshoremen's bar off Columbia Street, Red Hook, Brooklyn, fall 1970, a Knicks game night in the first-championship afterglow. On the television above the backbar a basket has just dropped and the whole room erupts: two dockworkers in work jackets embracing, a lifted beer slopping over a fist, the barmaid's hands thrown up, every face turned to the screen. At the far end of the rail the investigator sits alone, glass untouched, turned the other way, watching the front door in the backbar mirror. The light is the bar's own: red and blue beer signs, the television's grey flicker on the crowd, low bulbs over the backbar, smoke hanging in all of it. Grainy 35mm Eastman color negative, muted palette broken by the sign glow, full-bleed frame, no black bars, no text, no watermark.

stills.notes: Skeleton reframe of Hammett ch. 20 (the last interview before he hands her over) + Part 6: 'everyone sells out everyone for a brick of flour.' Distinct from the old spec's turning-her-in (the street handover): this is the interior instant the decision becomes visible on both faces — the look held too long, the receiver already off the cradle.
stills.prompt: The investigator's walk-up apartment off Court Street, Brooklyn, fall 1970, before dawn. He holds the dark-haired woman by the shoulders at arm's length and the look between them has gone on too long: her face is moving from pleading to understanding, his is fixed, finished arguing with himself. On the table behind him the black rotary phone sits with the receiver already lifted off the cradle. The light is mixed and cold: grey pre-dawn sky through the window on her face, the bare yellow hallway globe through the open apartment door edging his shoulder, nothing warm anywhere between them, the rest of the room in shadow. Grainy 35mm Eastman color negative, muted palette, full-bleed frame, no black bars, no text, no watermark.

stills.notes: Skeleton reframe of Hammett ch. 20, final page (the secretary's recoil after he turns the woman in), role per Part 2: 'the loyal secretary / the lead's conscience.' The refused touch is the verdict on his code — the cost of the ending carried in a flinch and a hand touching nothing.
stills.prompt: The second-floor office above the dry cleaner, Carroll Gardens, Brooklyn, fall 1970, the morning after he gave her up. The young secretary stands at the office window with her back half to him, face wet, arms wrapped around herself. The investigator has put a hand out to her shoulder and she has flinched away from it, and the hand hangs in the air between them, touching nothing. A folded morning newspaper lies on the steel desk. The desk lamp is off; the only light is flat overcast daylight through the office windows and the pale glow of the frosted-glass door, and the room reads cold. Grainy 35mm Eastman color negative, muted palette, full-bleed frame, no black bars, no text, no watermark.
